title: Parser-health dashboard: per-field null-rate trend, TargetUserName step-change
event_type: Null-rate monitoring panel, LinuxAuthEvents (sudo) log source, field-level trend for TargetUserName / user.target.name

fields.label: Step-Change Magnitude
fields.value: +99.4 points in a single day, no gradual drift

callouts.explanation: Establishes the flat, near-zero noise floor a healthy trend line holds for months, which is the reference point that makes the later jump visually obvious rather than a matter of interpretation.

This is the visible step-change the figure exists to illustrate: the field goes from consistently populated to consistently null in one ingest-pipeline upgrade, with no ramp-up period, matching the sudo-integration field rename described in Section 8.

Shows why a standing null-rate monitor catches this within one monitoring cycle instead of requiring someone to notice a rule has gone quiet, which is the operational payoff Section 7.1 claims for this monitoring pattern.
Ties the abstract null-rate metric back to the concrete rules it protects, showing the monitor is field-centric and catches the break independent of which specific rule references the field.

note: Conceptual/illustrative dashboard mockup depicting a null-rate trend and step-change; not a screenshot captured from any real SIEM or monitoring product interface.
